name: create-verification-skill
description: "Generate a project-local verify-<app> skill: a control.sh harness that launches the real app from an empty data dir, drives it the way a user does (HTTP, CLI), and keeps evidence, plus a feature map with one recipe per feature. Use for /create-verification-skill, \"make a verify skill for this repo\", or when agents have no scripted way to prove a change works in the running app."
---

# Create a verification skill

Give agents hands and eyes: one committed, scripted way to launch the app, drive a feature the way a user would, and keep proof. Write the output for the next agent, who reads it cold, mid-task, and has never seen the app.

10→`$SKILL_DIR` is the directory holding this file. Scripts are Python 3 stdlib and bash; each has `--help`.

## 1. Interview the repo, not the user

```bash
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/scan_repo.py .        # --json for the full inventory
```

Check each answer against the code. Ask the user only what the repo can't tell you.

20→- **Surface:** what a user touches (HTTP API, CLI, web UI, desktop app). Pick the primary one and note the rest.
- **Run:** the repo's own start command, ports, env vars, seed data, auth.
- **Drive:** existing harnesses first (e2e specs, curl-able routes, PTY scripts). Otherwise plain HTTP for services and a fresh process per CLI call.
- **Observe:** response bodies, stdout/stderr/exit codes, files written, rows inserted, logs.
- **Isolate:** can two instances run side by side (ports, data dirs)? If not, the skill says so and refuses to drive a shared instance.

If the checkout doesn't build or start, fix that or report it precisely before generating anything. A skill written against a broken base teaches wrong steps.

## 2. Scaffold

30→```bash
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/scaffold.py . --app <name>    # --skills-dir .cursor/skills for Cursor
```

This writes `.claude/skills/verify-<name>/`:

- `SKILL.md` with Launch, Doctor, Drive, Evidence, Cleanup, and Helpers sections.
- `features/README.md` plus one file per detected feature, each with four H2s in order: `Sub-features`, `How to get to it (user POV)`, `Driving it with control.sh`, `Gotchas`.
- `scripts/control.sh` with `launch | doctor | drive | evidence | cleanup | status | prove`. It keeps a pid file, kills only the process group it started after checking the leader's recorded start identity, and writes evidence to `artifacts/verify/<run-id>/`.

40→Anything the scan couldn't establish is a `TODO(verify):` marker. [`references/feature-example.md`](references/feature-example.md) shows a finished recipe.

## 3. Replace every TODO with real commands

```bash
grep -rn 'TODO(verify)' .claude/skills/verify-<name>
```

- Run each command before you write it down, and record the observed status or output as the expected result. Replace `<id>`-style placeholders in recipe commands with the values you observed; `check_verify_skill.py` fails on them.
- Launch must reach a usable state from an empty data dir, including migrations and seed data. Ready means usable, not just "the process answers". Keep a real read (`READ_PATH`) in doctor.
50→- Use stable handles: route paths, subcommand names, JSON fields, ARIA roles. Never coordinates or tab order.
- Evidence follows the real user path: the action, then the resulting state through a second view, then the side effect (`evidence --copy-data`). Mock only at production boundaries. Check what a dry-run mode really skips by observing it.
- If the seed data lacks a journey's precondition, the journey fails and the reason goes in that feature's Gotchas. Never weaken a journey to make it pass.
- An irrelevant missing asset that blocks startup may be created by the skill, marked as verification scaffolding, and removed in cleanup.
- Extend `control.sh` when the surface needs it (a browser or PTY subcommand). Keep every helper executable and show its invocation in SKILL.md.

## 4. Prove it end to end once

```bash
C=.claude/skills/verify-<name>/scripts/control.sh
60→$C launch && $C doctor && $C drive --feature <id> http GET <route> && $C evidence --copy-data && $C cleanup
ls artifacts/verify/<run-id>/              # the evidence must survive cleanup
$C prove --feature <id> http GET <route>    # the same sequence as one command
```

Drive one mapped feature exactly as its recipe says. Fix what fails, and run `cleanup` after every failed attempt so no process or port is left behind. A skill that was never executed is a draft, not a deliverable. If you proved it in a stand-in (a container instead of the real host), list the setup steps the stand-in did that the real target won't.

## 5. Gate and hand off

```bash
70→python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/check_verify_skill.py .claude/skills/verify-<name>    # must exit 0
```

Commit the skill so every person and agent drives the app the same way, and add `artifacts/` to `.gitignore`. Point the user at /maintain-verification-skill to keep the map honest. Suggest a cadence only if asked.

**Reply:** the surface you chose, the prove command and its output, the evidence path, features mapped vs. detected, and anything left unverified with the reason.

## Sources

Adapted from pstack by Lauren Tan (MIT, © 2026 Lauren Tan). The scripts are new to poteto-skills.

- S13 Guide 06, verify and ship (control CLI traits, prove before handoff): https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/docs/guide/06-verify-and-ship.md
- S17 principle-prove-it-works: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md

- S1 inverted pyramid post ("use it minimally, but do use /create-verification-skill"): https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985

"""Scaffold a project-local verification skill from scan_repo.py's inventory.

  scaffold.py REPO --app NAME [--skills-dir .claude/skills] [--force] [--max-features N] [--json]

Writes REPO/<skills-dir>/verify-NAME/:
  SKILL.md               frontmatter + Launch, Doctor, Drive, Evidence, Cleanup, Helpers
  features/README.md     the map index: preconditions, conventions, proof rules, feature list
  features/<id>.md       one per detected feature, four H2s in order:
10→                         Sub-features / How to get to it (user POV) / Driving it with control.sh / Gotchas
  scripts/control.sh     launch | doctor | drive | evidence | cleanup | status | prove
                         (pid file, kills only the process group it started, evidence in artifacts/verify/<run-id>/)

Every value the scan could not establish becomes a `TODO(verify): ...` marker.
check_verify_skill.py fails until each one is replaced with a real command or fact.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
20→import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True  # importing scan_repo must not leave __pycache__ in the skill dir
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import scan_repo  # noqa: E402
30→
TODO = "TODO(verify)"


def sh(value: str) -> str:
    return shlex.quote(value)


def pick_server(inv: dict) -> dict | None:
    return next((lc for lc in inv["launch_candidates"] if lc["kind"] == "server"), None)
40→

def pick_cli(inv: dict) -> dict | None:
    return next((lc for lc in inv["launch_candidates"] if lc["kind"] == "cli"), None)


def launch_command(lc: dict | None, inv: dict) -> tuple[str, str, int | None, list[str]]:
    """(LAUNCH_CMD, PORT_MODE, DEFAULT_PORT, todos)."""
    todos: list[str] = []
    if lc is None:
50→        return "", "none", None, todos
    env_names = {e["name"] for e in inv["env_vars"]}
    prog, sub = lc.get("prog"), lc.get("subcommand")
    head = f"{prog} " if prog else ""
    pre, post = [], []
    if lc.get("data_flag"):
        (pre if lc.get("data_flag_global") else post).append(f'{lc["data_flag"]} "$DATA_DIR"')
    if lc.get("port_flag"):
        (pre if lc.get("port_flag_global") else post).append(f'{lc["port_flag"]} "$PORT"')
    if prog and sub:
60→        cmd = " ".join([prog, *pre, sub, *post])
    else:
        cmd = " ".join([lc["cmd"], *pre, *post]).strip() if not head else lc["cmd"]
    if lc.get("port_flag"):
        mode = "flag"
    elif "PORT" in env_names:
        mode = "env"
    elif lc.get("port"):
        mode = "fixed"
    else:
70→        mode = "flag"
        todos.append("port")
        cmd += f" {TODO}: pass $PORT so the app listens where control.sh expects"
    if not lc.get("data_flag"):
        data_env = [n for n in sorted(env_names) if re.search(r"DATA|DB|DIR|STORE|STATE|HOME|PATH", n) and n != "PORT"]
        hint = f" (env {', '.join(data_env)}?)" if data_env else ""
        todos.append("data")
        cmd += f" {TODO}: point the app at the empty $DATA_DIR{hint}"
    return cmd, mode, lc.get("port"), todos

80→
def cli_base(cli: dict | None, inv: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(prog with data flag placed correctly, data_flag_text after subcommand)."""
    if cli is None:
        return "", ""
    prog = cli["cmd"]
    if cli.get("data_flag"):
        if cli.get("data_flag_global"):
            return f"{prog} {cli['data_flag']} {{DATA_DIR}}", ""
        return prog, f" {cli['data_flag']} {{DATA_DIR}}"
90→    return prog, ""


def sample_value(name: str, fid: str) -> str:
    n = name.lower()
    if n in ("id", "todo_id", "item_id", "pk") or n.endswith("_id"):
        return f"<{name}>"
    if n in ("done", "completed", "archived", "enabled"):
        return "true"
    if n in ("count", "limit", "priority", "n"):
100→        return "1"
    return f"verify {fid}"


def concrete(path: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"<\*>|<([^>]*)>", lambda m: "<" + (m.group(1) or "id") + ">", path)


def feature_md(f: dict, inv: dict, C: str, cli_prefix: str, cli_suffix: str, list_route: dict | None,
               list_cmd: dict | None) -> str:
110→    title, fid = f["title"], f["id"]
    lines = [f"# {title}", "",
             f"{TODO}: one paragraph, from the user's point of view: what \"{title.lower()}\" does and what the user "
             f"sees afterwards.", "", "## Sub-features", ""]
    for r in f["routes"]:
        lines.append(f"- `{fid}-http-{r['method'].lower()}`: `{r['method']} {concrete(r['path'])}` over HTTP.")
    for c in f["commands"]:
        lines.append(f"- `{fid}-cli-{c['name']}`: `{c['prog']} {c['name']}` in a terminal.")
    lines += ["", "## How to get to it (user POV)", ""]
    for r in f["routes"]:
120→        lines.append(f"- HTTP API: `{r['method']} {concrete(r['path'])}` on the running server (base URL from `launch`).")
    for c in f["commands"]:
        args = " ".join(f"<{p}>" for p in c.get("positionals", []))
        lines.append(f"- Terminal: `{' '.join(x for x in (c['prog'], c['name'], args) if x)}`.")
    lines += ["", "## Driving it with control.sh", "", "Preconditions:", "",
              f"- `{C} doctor` exits 0."]
    needs_existing = f["action"] not in ("create", "list") or any("<" in r["path"] for r in f["routes"])
    if needs_existing:
        lines.append(f"- At least one {scan_repo.singular(f['resource'])} exists: run the create recipe first. "
                     f"{TODO}: the id it returns on an empty data dir.")
130→    else:
        lines.append("- Fresh run from `launch` (empty data dir).")
    lines.append("")
    for r in f["routes"]:
        path = concrete(r["path"])
        body = ""
        if r["method"] in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH") and f["action"] in ("create", "update"):
            keys = r.get("body_keys") or []
            if keys:
                body = " " + sh(json.dumps({k: sample_value(k, fid) for k in keys}))
140→            else:
                body = f" '{TODO}: JSON body'"
        id_note = f" Replace `<...>` with the real id. " if "<" in path else " "
        lines.append(f"- **HTTP {r['method']}.** Run `{C} drive --feature {fid} http {r['method']} {path}{body}`."
                     f"{id_note}{TODO}: the expected status and body.")
    for c in f["commands"]:
        args = " ".join(sh(sample_value(p, fid)) for p in c.get("positionals", []))
        cmdline = f"{cli_prefix} {c['name']}{cli_suffix} {args}".strip()
        id_note = " Replace `<...>` with the real id." if "<" in args else ""
        lines.append(f"- **CLI {c['name']}.** Run `{C} drive --feature {fid} cli -- {cmdline}`.{id_note} "
150→                     f"{TODO}: the expected exit code and stdout.")
    proof = []
    if list_route:
        proof.append(f"`{C} drive --feature {fid} http GET {concrete(list_route['path'])}`")
    elif list_cmd:
        proof.append(f"`{C} drive --feature {fid} cli -- {cli_prefix} {list_cmd['name']}{cli_suffix}`".replace("  ", " "))
    proof.append(f"`{C} evidence --copy-data`")
    lines.append(f"- **Proof.** Read it back through a second view: run {' and '.join(proof)}. "

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

import shlex

def sh(value: str) -> str:
    return shlex.quote(value)


def pick_server(inv: dict) -> dict | None:
    return next((lc for lc in inv["launch_candidates"] if lc["kind"] == "server"), None)


def pick_cli(inv: dict) -> dict | None:
    return next((lc for lc in inv["launch_candidates"] if lc["kind"] == "cli"), None)


def launch_command(lc: dict | None, inv: dict) -> tuple[str, str, int | None, list[str]]:
    """(LAUNCH_CMD, PORT_MODE, DEFAULT_PORT, todos)."""
    todos: list[str] = []
    if lc is None:
        return "", "none", None, todos
    env_names = {e["name"] for e in inv["env_vars"]}
    prog, sub = lc.get("prog"), lc.get("subcommand")
    head = f"{prog} " if prog else ""
    pre, post = [], []
    if lc.get("data_flag"):
        (pre if lc.get("data_flag_global") else post).append(f'{lc["data_flag"]} "$DATA_DIR"')
    if lc.get("port_flag"):
        (pre if lc.get("port_flag_global") else post).append(f'{lc["port_flag"]} "$PORT"')
    if prog and sub:
        cmd = " ".join([prog, *pre, sub, *post])
    else:
        cmd = " ".join([lc["cmd"], *pre, *post]).strip() if not head else lc["cmd"]
    if lc.get("port_flag"):
        mode = "flag"
    elif "PORT" in env_names:
        mode = "env"
    elif lc.get("port"):
        mode = "fixed"
    else:
        mode = "flag"
        todos.append("port")
        cmd += f" {TODO}: pass $PORT so the app listens where control.sh expects"
    if not lc.get("data_flag"):
        data_env = [n for n in sorted(env_names) if re.search(r"DATA|DB|DIR|STORE|STATE|HOME|PATH", n) and n != "PORT"]
        hint = f" (env {', '.join(data_env)}?)" if data_env else ""
        todos.append("data")
        cmd += f" {TODO}: point the app at the empty $DATA_DIR{hint}"
    return cmd, mode, lc.get("port"), todos


def cli_base(cli: dict | None, inv: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(prog with data flag placed correctly, data_flag_text after subcommand)."""
    if cli is None:
        return "", ""
    prog = cli["cmd"]
    if cli.get("data_flag"):
        if cli.get("data_flag_global"):
            return f"{prog} {cli['data_flag']} {{DATA_DIR}}", ""
        return prog, f" {cli['data_flag']} {{DATA_DIR}}"
    return prog, ""


def sample_value(name: str, fid: str) -> str:
    n = name.lower()
    if n in ("id", "todo_id", "item_id", "pk") or n.endswith("_id"):
        return f"<{name}>"
    if n in ("done", "completed", "archived", "enabled"):
        return "true"
    if n in ("count", "limit", "priority", "n"):
        return "1"
    return f"verify {fid}"


def concrete(path: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"<\*>|<([^>]*)>", lambda m: "<" + (m.group(1) or "id") + ">", path)


def feature_md(f: dict, inv: dict, C: str, cli_prefix: str, cli_suffix: str, list_route: dict | None,
               list_cmd: dict | None) -> str:
    title, fid = f["title"], f["id"]
    lines = [f"# {title}", "",
             f"{TODO}: one paragraph, from the user's point of view: what \"{title.lower()}\" does and what the user "
             f"sees afterwards.", "", "## Sub-features", ""]
    for r in f["routes"]:
        lines.append(f"- `{fid}-http-{r['method'].lower()}`: `{r['method']} {concrete(r['path'])}` over HTTP.")
    for c in f["commands"]:
        lines.append(f"- `{fid}-cli-{c['name']}`: `{c['prog']} {c['name']}` in a terminal.")
    lines += ["", "## How to get to it (user POV)", ""]
    for r in f["routes"]:
        lines.append(f"- HTTP API: `{r['method']} {concrete(r['path'])}` on the running server (base URL from `launch`).")
    for c in f["commands"]:
        args = " ".join(f"<{p}>" for p in c.get("positionals", []))
        lines.append(f"- Terminal: `{' '.join(x for x in (c['prog'], c['name'], args) if x)}`.")
    lines += ["", "## Driving it with control.sh", "", "Preconditions:", "",
              f"- `{C} doctor` exits 0."]
    needs_existing = f["action"] not in ("create", "list") or any("<" in r["path"] for r in f["routes"])
    if needs_existing:
        lines.append(f"- At least one {scan_repo.singular(f['resource'])} exists: run the create recipe first. "
                     f"{TODO}: the id it returns on an empty data dir.")
    else:
        lines.append("- Fresh run from `launch` (empty data dir).")
    lines.append("")
    for r in f["routes"]:
        path = concrete(r["path"])
        body = ""
        if r["method"] in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH") and f["action"] in ("create", "update"):
            keys = r.get("body_keys") or []
            if keys:
                body = " " + sh(json.dumps({k: sample_value(k, fid) for k in keys}))
            else:
                body = f" '{TODO}: JSON body'"
        id_note = f" Replace `<...>` with the real id. " if "<" in path else " "
        lines.append(f"- **HTTP {r['method']}.** Run `{C} drive --feature {fid} http {r['method']} {path}{body}`."
                     f"{id_note}{TODO}: the expected status and body.")
    for c in f["commands"]:
        args = " ".join(sh(sample_value(p, fid)) for p in c.get("positionals", []))
        cmdline = f"{cli_prefix} {c['name']}{cli_suffix} {args}".strip()
        id_note = " Replace `<...>` with the real id." if "<" in args else ""
        lines.append(f"- **CLI {c['name']}.** Run `{C} drive --feature {fid} cli -- {cmdline}`.{id_note} "
                     f"{TODO}: the expected exit code and stdout.")
    proof = []
    if list_route:
        proof.append(f"`{C} drive --feature {fid} http GET {concrete(list_route['path'])}`")
    elif list_cmd:
        proof.append(f"`{C} drive --feature {fid} cli -- {cli_prefix} {list_cmd['name']}{cli_suffix}`".replace("  ", " "))
    proof.append(f"`{C} evidence --copy-data`")
    lines.append(f"- **Proof.** Read it back through a second view: run {' and '.join(proof)}. "
                 f"{TODO}: what the read-back and the data snapshot must show.")
    lines += ["", "## Gotchas", "",
              f"- {TODO}: traps that waste or invalidate a run here (ids, ordering, defaults, validation)."]
    if cli_prefix and "{DATA_DIR}" in (cli_prefix + cli_suffix):
        lines.append("- Every CLI call needs the run's data dir (`{DATA_DIR}`); without it the CLI touches its default "
                     "data location instead of the scratch one.")
        flag = re.search(r"(--[\w-]+) \{DATA_DIR\}", cli_prefix + cli_suffix)
        if flag and flag.group(1) in ("--db", "--database", "--db-path", "--file", "--path", "--store", "--data-path"):
            lines.append(f"- {TODO}: confirm `{flag.group(1)}` takes a directory. If it takes a file, pass "
                         f"`{{DATA_DIR}}/<file>` everywhere instead.")
    elif f["commands"]:
        lines.append(f"- {TODO}: confirm where CLI commands store data; drives must not touch real user data.")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def readme_md(app: str, feats: list[dict], C: str, skipped: list[dict]) -> str:
    lines = [f"# {app} verification map", "",
             f"The maintained source for verifying what {app} users can do. Read this index before driving the app, "
             "then follow the matching feature file as the recipe.", "",
             "## Baseline preconditions", "",
             f"- Launch with `{C} launch`: empty data dir, its own port, JSON with run_id, base_url, data_dir.",
             f"- `{C} doctor` exits 0 before the first drive.",
             "- Never drive an instance this run did not start.",
             f"- {TODO}: seed data the journeys need, created through the app's own routes or commands (or \"none\").",
             "", "## Driving conventions", "",
             "- Run every command from the repo root, literally as written.",
             f"- HTTP: `{C} drive --feature <id> http METHOD PATH ['JSON'] [--expect STATUS]`.",
             f"- CLI: `{C} drive --feature <id> cli -- <command>`. `{{DATA_DIR}}`, `{{PORT}}`, `{{BASE_URL}}`, and "
             "`{RUN_ID}` in arguments become this run's values.",
             "- Start each recipe from the state its Preconditions name. Use stable handles: route paths, subcommand "
             "names, JSON fields.",
             "", "## Proof and skip reporting", "",
             "- Each drive records the action and its result in `artifacts/verify/<run-id>/`.",
             f"- A mutation needs a read-only second view (a GET or a list command), then `{C} evidence --copy-data` "
             "for the stored side effect.",
             "- Record the feature id with every artifact (`--feature`).",
             "- Report an unreachable path with the attempted command and the unmet precondition. Never report it as "
             "verified through a different path.",
             "", "## Feature entry contract", "",
             "Each feature file has an H1, one paragraph of user-visible behavior, then exactly these H2s in order: "
             "`Sub-features`, `How to get to it (user POV)`, `Driving it with control.sh`, `Gotchas`. Keep "
             "implementation details out: user paths, stable handles, required state, commands, observable proof.",
             "", "## Features", ""]
    for f in feats:
        entry = [f"`{r['method']} {concrete(r['path'])}`" for r in f["routes"]] + \
                [f"`{c['prog']} {c['name']}`" for c in f["commands"]]
        lines.append(f"- [{f['title']}](./{f['id']}.md): " + ", ".join(entry) + ".")
    if not feats:
        lines.append(f"- {TODO}: no routes or commands were detected. Add one file per user-facing feature.")
    if skipped:
        lines += ["", "## Not mapped yet", ""]
        lines += [f"- {f['title']} (`{f['id']}`): over --max-features; add a file when it matters." for f in skipped]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    lines = ["---", f"name: verify-{app}", f"description: {json.dumps(desc)}", "---", "",

    if launch:
        ready = f"`GET {health}` returns 2xx" if health else "the port accepts connections"

    else:

            continue
        out.append(target.split("#", 1)[0])
    return [t for t in out if t]


def index_report(skill: Path) -> dict:
    """missing (feature file not indexed), dead (link to nothing), duplicate, extra (link to a non-feature file)."""
    readme = skill / "features" / "README.md"
    rep = {"missing": [], "dead": [], "duplicate": [], "extra": []}
    if not readme.is_file():
        return rep
    feats = {p.resolve() for p in feature_files(skill)}
    seen = set()
    for target in local_links(readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")):
        p = (readme.parent / target).resolve()
        if not p.exists():
            rep["dead"].append(target)
        elif p in seen and p in feats:
            rep["duplicate"].append(target)
        elif p not in feats and p.suffix == ".md" and p.parent == readme.parent.resolve():
            rep["extra"].append(target)
        seen.add(p)
    rep["missing"] = sorted(p.name for p in feats if p not in seen)
    return rep


def check(skill: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Return a list of {check, ok, detail}."""
    results: list[dict] = []

    def add(name: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
        results.append({"check": name, "ok": ok, "detail": detail})

    sk = skill / "SKILL.md"
    if not sk.is_file():
        add("SKILL.md exists", False, f"{sk} not found")
        return results
    text = sk.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    fm = frontmatter(text)
    if fm is None:
        add("frontmatter", False, "SKILL.md must start with --- YAML frontmatter --- (without it the skill never registers)")
    else:
        missing = [k for k in ("name", "description") if not fm.get(k)]
        add("frontmatter", not missing, "missing " + ", ".join(missing) if missing else f"name={fm['name']}")
        if fm.get("name"):
            add("name matches dir", fm["name"] == skill.name, f"name={fm['name']} dir={skill.name}")
    h2 = [t for _, t in headings(text, 2)]
    for sec in REQUIRED_SECTIONS:
        present = any(t == sec or t.startswith(sec + " ") or t.startswith(sec + ":") for t in h2)
        add(f"section {sec}", present, "" if present else f"add a `## {sec}` section")
    for target in local_links(text):
        p = (skill / target)
        add(f"SKILL.md link {target}", p.exists(), "" if p.exists() else "dead link")

    readme = skill / "features" / "README.md"
    add("features/README.md exists", readme.is_file(), "" if readme.is_file() else "create the feature map index")
    feats = feature_files(skill)
    add("feature files", bool(feats), f"{len(feats)} file(s)" if feats else "add one file per user-facing feature")
    for f in feats:
        ftext = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        errs = h2_contract_errors(ftext)
        add(f"contract {f.name}", not errs, "; ".join(errs))
        holes = recipe_placeholders(ftext)
        add(f"literal recipes {f.name}", not holes,
            f"placeholder(s) {', '.join(holes)} in a drive command; write the real value" if holes else "")
    idx = index_report(skill)
    for kind in ("dead", "missing", "duplicate", "extra"):
        vals = idx[kind]
        add(f"index {kind}", not vals, ", ".join(vals) if vals else "")

    todos = []
    for p in sorted(skill.rglob("*")):
        if p.is_file() and "__pycache__" not in p.parts and p.suffix not in (".pyc", ".pyo") and p.stat().st_size < 2_000_000:
            for n, line in enumerate(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1):
                if TODO in line:
                    todos.append(f"{p.relative_to(skill).as_posix()}:{n}")
    add("no TODO(verify) left", not todos, (f"{len(todos)}: " + ", ".join(todos[:12]) + (" …" if len(todos) > 12 else ""))
        if todos else "")

    scripts = sorted(p for p in (skill / "scripts").rglob("*") if p.is_file() and "__pycache__" not in p.parts and p.suffix not in (".pyc", ".pyo")) if (skill / "scripts").is_dir() else []
    for s in scripts:
        rel = s.relative_to(skill).as_posix()
        execable = os.access(s, os.X_OK)
        add(f"executable {rel}", execable, "" if execable else f"chmod +x {rel}")
        head = s.read_bytes()[:2]
        add(f"shebang {rel}", head == b"#!", "" if head == b"#!" else "first line must be #!/usr/bin/env ...")
        if s.suffix in (".sh", ".bash"):
            r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-n", str(s)], capture_output=True, text=True)
            add(f"bash -n {rel}", r.returncode == 0, r.stderr.strip()[:200])
        if s.suffix == ".py":
            try:
                compile(s.read_bytes(), str(s), "exec")
                add(f"compile {rel}", True)
            except (SyntaxError, ValueError) as e:
                add(f"compile {rel}", False, str(e)[:200])
        mentioned = rel in text or s.name in text
        add(f"documented {rel}", mentioned, "" if mentioned else "show its invocation in SKILL.md (Helpers)")
    return results


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="check_verify_skill.py",
        description="Check a verify-<app> skill: frontmatter, Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup/Helpers sections, "
                    "feature files with the four ordered H2s, live index links, no TODO(verify) left, and executable, "
                    "documented scripts. Exit 1 on any failure.",
        epilog="example:\n  check_verify_skill.py .claude/skills/verify-todo",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    ap.add_argument("skill_dir", type=Path, help="the verify-<app> skill directory")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="machine-readable output")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.skill_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"check_verify_skill: {args.skill_dir} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    results = check(args.skill_dir)
    failed = [r for r in results if not r["ok"]]
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"skill_dir": str(args.skill_dir), "ok": not failed, "failed": len(failed),
                          "results": results}, indent=2))
    else:
        for r in results:
            if not r["ok"]:
                print(f"FAIL  {r['check']}: {r['detail']}")
        print(f"check_verify_skill: {'PASS' if not failed else 'FAIL'} ({len(results) - len(failed)}/{len(results)} checks)"
              f" {args.skill_dir}")
    return 0 if not failed else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

name: long-running-background-tasks
description: >-
  Required reading before you start, watch, or wait on anything that keeps running after you launch it — background jobs, watchers, scheduled loops, CI, pull requests, training runs, dev servers, long builds. Read it before you launch such work and before you report on its state. Saying where a running job stands counts as working on it. Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.
---

# Working with long-running background tasks

Only submitting or queuing jobs is not sufficient to complete the task. The definition of done is the job has completed successfully and you have verified that it has produced all the expected outputs.
10→
This means you must see through the jobs completion by watching the job to ensure that its healthy, progressing, and working as intended.

## Tools available

There's two ways to watch jobs: monitor and loop. Decide which of the two you need, sometimes you need both.

### monitor — deterministic, actionable events

- Use a monitor when the event is a predicate a script can evaluate — an API response, an exit code, a port answering.
20→- Typical events: CI turning red, a PR comment or merge conflict, a PR becoming ready to merge, a dev server coming up or going down, a job reaching a terminal state.
- The monitor requires a script polls on a fixed cadence and stays silent until the predicate fires, so an idle job costs nothing. More on writing good monitoring scripts below.
- Examples of when to use:
  - Monitoring a PR — wake on CI breaking, merge conflicts, etc.
  - Checking if local tooling is up — wake on the service being unavailable, errors, etc.
  - All of these wakeup cases can be checked deterministically.

### loop — qualitative health that needs reading

- Use a loop when judging health requires reading the logs and system information to detect failing, faulty or stalled jobs. It uses a subagent which is more expensive but more thorough.
30→- Typical signals: the loss curve going unstable, a filtering pipeline producing garbage, throughput quietly degrading, faulty nodes throwing CUDA errors.
- A subagent reads the logs on a fixed cadence (say every 10 min) and reports what changed, so it costs a wakeup every cycle.
- Examples of when to use:
  - Checking on a training or data processing job — the subagent should scan for instability, degradation, faulty nodes, etc.
  - Monitoring system deployment health — the subagent should scan for 4xx/5xx, response times, resources, etc.
  - All of these wakeup cases are hard to describe deterministically and hard to fully enumerate, so it is better to use a subagent to validate.

## Good monitoring scripts

The monitor tool wakes you up every time you log to stdout. Wakeups are expensive, so only log if there is something actionable — but log it as early as possible, since staying silent delays the task. Plan accordingly: minimize the number of wakeups while still firing them as quickly as possible.
40→
### Planning

- Enumerate all terminal conditions.
  - For PRs, this includes the PR being merged or closed.
  - For long-running jobs, this includes the job completing or unrecoverable failures.
- Enumerate all other situations where a wakeup is needed.
  - For PRs, this would include when a comment arrives (there are four different types of PR comments), when CI fails, when a merge conflict arises, and when the PR becomes ready to merge (CI green, no conflicts, reviews complete, no blockers).
  - For an ML training job, this can be when the loss is unstable or the instance is preempted.
- Determine situations where the monitoring has to update what it is tracking. For example, for monitoring PRs, the latest commit hash may change as you push new commits.
50→
### Writing

- The monitoring script should poll every 30s. `watch_pr.py` defaults to
  `--poll-interval 30`. Lower intervals cause GitHub rate limits, especially
  with more than one watcher on the same token.
- Based on the planning, exit immediately on terminal conditions with FAILED, DONE, or CANCELLED, and log ACTION_REQUIRED for wakeups.
- Send all debug diagnostics — both your watcher's own trace and the monitored job's output — to a file, so a log line can never be mistaken for DONE, FAILED, or CANCELLED.
- The script should fail as early as possible. Emit a FAILED token immediately when any required condition reaches terminal failure. For example, if you are waiting on CI and any of them fail, emit FAILED immediately.
- Write the script to a durable location such as ~/.grok and name it something clear such as `ci_watcher.sh`.
60→- Key every log file the script writes on the pid or session id of the thing being watched. The paths are otherwise fixed, so a second job of the same kind silently clobbers the first one's log.

## Handling wake-ups

- Address errors or actionable events immediately. Look through the logs and debug the issue thoroughly before settling on a root cause, as long-running processes are generally expensive. Resubmit the job once it is fixed:
  - For PRs, this means repushing the changes and restarting CI (if needed).
  - For jobs, requeue or relaunch the job.
  - Always restart the monitor or loop so that it points at the new PR or job.
- If there are multiple jobs running, start debugging immediately when any jobs fail. Minimize total wall-time with completing tasks.

70→## Restarts

- Whenever you relaunch a job, always update the monitor.
- Monitors have a maximum 10-hour time limit, so be sure to restart them if you hit the time limit and if the task being monitored is still running.
- When you spawn a new monitor, make sure to kill any previous ones that the new one replaces. For example, if you fix a training run and respawn it, be sure to kill previous monitors, as irrelevant wakeups are expensive.

## Cleanup

- If a monitor is in a terminal state, kill the monitor, the loop, and the job. Dangling processes such as unkilled broken training runs are expensive. Then, address all issues if present.
- If an outdated monitor wakes you — that is, it is attached to an old or dead run — make sure to kill it.
80→- Do not leave detached workers, duplicate pollers, or orphaned watcher processes behind.

## Examples

### Example: maintaining a dev server

Suppose you just made some changes to the user's frontend code and would like to spin it up to test it. While you're testing it, you would like to know if the server goes down for any reason (if you made changes, for example). This is a great use case for the monitor tool. First start a React app in a background terminal, which reports its pid:

```
run_terminal_command(
90→  command="echo $$; npm start >~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/dev_server_$$.log 2>&1",
  timeout=0,
  description="Start the dev server on :3000",
  background=true
) # prints the pid 123456789
```

There are no terminal states, but there are two actionable events from the watcher: `http://localhost:3000` coming up and going down.

You want to be notified as soon as it is up so you can use it, and you want to be woken when it stops so you can address it — fix the code, restart the server, free the port. Both down paths quote the tail of the server's log, so the wakeup arrives with the error already in hand. Polling every 5s is a good cadence since you want to quickly fix it if it is down, and it is not expensive to poll.
100→
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log paths are keyed on the server pid so two dev servers cannot clobber each other.
PID=$1 URL=http://localhost:3000 DIR=~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks
LOG=$DIR/dev_server_$PID.log
up() { curl -fsS -o /dev/null --max-time 5 "$URL" 2>>"$DIR/watch_dev_server_$PID.log"; }
why() { tail -20 "$LOG" | tr -d '\r' | tr '\n' ' '; }

until up; do
110→  kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || { echo "FAILED: pid $PID exited before $URL came up: $(why)"; exit 1; }
  sleep 5
done
echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: $URL is up"

while :; do
  sleep 5
  up || { echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: $URL is down: $(why)"; until up; do sleep 5; done; }
done
```
120→
To spawn the monitor, point it at the pid `npm start` reported:

```
monitor(
  command='bash ~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/watch_dev_server.sh 123456789',
  description="Watch the dev server on :3000"
)
```

130→On the first wakeup the app is ready to use and you can start testing it. After that, you may be woken up if the server goes down. When you do:
- Read `~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/dev_server_<pid>.log` for the full compile error or port conflict and fix it.
- If the dev server survived, hot reload picks the fix up and the watcher recovers on its own, so leave the monitor running.
- If the process is dead, restart it with a fresh `run_terminal_command`, then kill this monitor and spawn a new one against the new pid.

### Example: PR monitoring

PR monitoring should stop when the PR is merged or closed, and it should wake up on:
- For comments, you should ask users how they would like to resolve them (which ones to address automatically, whether to respond / resolve, etc.), then store the decision for new future sessions. There are four different types of PR comments.
  - Inline review threads
140→  - Review bodies
  - Conversation comments
  - Commit comments
- Failing CI - most can be fixed in the code but sometimes they may be flaky. For flaky CI, just rerun them.
- Merge conflicts
- The PR becoming ready to merge — CI passes, no merge conflicts, reviews complete, no blockers, no unresolved inline threads. That wakeup is `kind: mergeable`. Tell the user they can merge now. It is not terminal; keep watching until merge or close.

You can find the example script bundled with this skill at watch_pr.py. It needs an authenticated `gh` CLI (`gh auth login`) and `python3`. Default poll is 30s; a lower poll rate may hit GitHub rate limits at higher concurrency. Transport errors (timeouts, resets, DNS) retry with backoff and jitter and do not print a line.

```
150→monitor(
  command='python3 ~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/watch_pr.py "https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/pull/123"',
  description="Watch PR 123"
)
```

### Example: training monitoring

For monitoring long training jobs, the terminal conditions are when the job either fails or completes. Further, many issues cannot be caught deterministically, so use a subagent to run a script for most of the high-level update, then scan the logs for errors such as faulty nodes or CUDA warnings.

160→The script below is bundled with this skill as watch_training.py. Run it with `--help` for every flag and for the run-directory and log-line layout it expects, since it parses nanoGPT stdout out of a Slurm run dir.

```md
Keep an eye on the nanoGPT run nanogpt_owt_124m_r1 (slurm job 1234567) and tell me what changed since last time. Worktree ~/worktrees/nanogpt-owt-124m.

1. python3 ~/.grok/skills/long-running-background-tasks/watch_training.py --run-name nanogpt_owt_124m_r1 --job-id 1234567 --target-val 3.00

How to report:
- Start with the job's state and if it changed, e.g. "still RUNNING" or "PENDING -> RUNNING".
- Copy the ISSUES line and the STATUS line from the monitor exactly as it is written, numbers and all. STATUS will include where the run is heading: how far along, iters left, the eta, and whether val loss is still coming down. We want val loss at or under 3.00.
170→- If the state didn't change, tell me that in one line and stop.
- If the job has finished or died, give me the state, the exit code, and the last ISSUES, and run these two for me:
  sacct -j 1234567 -D -X -P -o JobID,State,ExitCode,DerivedExitCode,Elapsed,NodeList,FailedNode
  tail -20 ~/train_logs/slurm-nanogpt_owt_124m_r1-1234567.out

Keep <=10 lines: state, progress and eta, loss trend, then anything that smells like training going unstable (loss spiking, NaN, val loss creeping back up) or the cluster misbehaving (a drained or failing node, OOM, NCCL errors, a preemption, iters suddenly slower than usual).
```

Launch the scheduler on a 10 min interval, and spawn a monitor to be notified when the job crashes or succeeds.

180→```
scheduler_create(
  interval="10m",
  prompt: "...", # Copy from the prompt above.
)
monitor(
  # Wakes on pending/running/finished changes after the first observation.
  # First poll is silent unless the job is already COMPLETED or failed —
  # PENDING matches *ING, so treating an empty previous state as a
  # transition would wake immediately on a just-submitted job.
190→  command='J=1234567; p=; while :; do s=$(sacct -nXP -j $J -o State|head -1); s=${s%% *}; s=${s:-PENDING}; if [ "$s" != "$p" ]; then case $s in COMPLETED) echo "DONE: $J"; exit;; PENDING|RUNNING|CONFIGURING|COMPLETING|REQUEUED|SUSPENDED|RESIZING) [ -n "$p" ] && echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: $J $p -> $s";; *) echo "FAILED: $J $s"; exit 1;; esac; fi; p=$s; sleep 30; done',
  description="Watch training run"
)
```

Launch both, so that we know when the job completes. When the monitor reports that the job has completed, cancel both the monitor and the scheduler, then determine next steps. Then:
- If it succeeded, simply present the results to the user.
- If it failed, debug the issue thoroughly, then fix and relaunch the job with new monitors attached. Make sure to have a thorough understanding of the issue before resubmitting, since training jobs are expensive. But always relaunch jobs so you don't waste the user's time.

# Working with long-running background tasks

Only submitting or queuing jobs is not sufficient to complete the task. The definition of done is the job has completed successfully and you have verified that it has produced all the expected outputs.

This means you must see through the jobs completion by watching the job to ensure that its healthy, progressing, and working as intended.

There's two ways to watch jobs: monitor and loop. Decide which of the two you need, sometimes you need both.

  - Checking if local tooling is up — wake on the service being unavailable, errors, etc.
  - All of these wakeup cases can be checked deterministically.

HEALTH_PATH is /web/index.html and READ_PATH is /web/data/garden-summary.json. PORT_MODE is env with DEFAULT_PORT set to 0.

A thirty-second ready timeout is sufficient because the export step is fast. The launch-site.sh script needs execute permissions. Python 3.13 http.server will bind to localhost using --directory, keeping the garden private.

Fixture creation is handled by launch-site.sh and documented in SKILL.md so it is reproducible. The script itself is the authoritative source, but SKILL.md must also describe what it writes so an agent can understand the setup without reading only the script. Because launch creates a fresh DATA_DIR each time, seeding once is sufficient; re-running the script is safe since it uses ln -sfn. If scan fails during launch, the server will not start. For the doctor command, a missing state directory in a fresh fake home should trigger a warning but still return ok=true.

The manual-jsonl adapter is "available" without the flag and "active" with it. The proof will use the fixture to show it as active while other adapters remain available, avoiding any real directory touches. An empty home should not trigger discovery of other adapters, but the command output will confirm this.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the agent-garden CLI only against a disposable HOME.
# Refuses the real user home so a verify drive cannot scan ~/.claude, ~/.codex, or ~/.cursor.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../.." && pwd)"
BIN="$REPO_ROOT/target/debug/agent-garden"

if [[ ! -x "$BIN" ]]; then
  echo "verify: missing $BIN" >&2
  echo "verify: build with: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build -p local-agent-garden-cli" >&2
  exit 127
fi

real_home="$(getent passwd "$(id -un)" | awk -F: '{print $6}')"
if [[ -z "${real_home}" || ! -d "$real_home" ]]; then
  echo "verify: could not resolve the real user home; refusing to run" >&2
  exit 2
fi
real_phys="$(cd "$real_home" && pwd -P)"

if [[ -z "${HOME:-}" || ! -d "$HOME" ]]; then
  echo "verify: HOME must be an existing disposable directory; refusing to scan the real home" >&2
  exit 2
fi
home_phys="$(cd "$HOME" && pwd -P)"
if [[ "$home_phys" == "$real_phys" || "$home_phys" == "$real_phys"/* ]]; then
  echo "verify: refusing HOME=$home_phys (inside the real user home)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ -z "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-}" || ! -d "$XDG_DATA_HOME" ]]; then
  echo "verify: XDG_DATA_HOME must be an existing disposable directory" >&2
  exit 2
fi
xdg_phys="$(cd "$XDG_DATA_HOME" && pwd -P)"
if [[ "$xdg_phys" == "$real_phys" || "$xdg_phys" == "$real_phys"/* ]]; then
  echo "verify: refusing XDG_DATA_HOME=$xdg_phys (inside the real user home)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

export HOME="$home_phys"
export XDG_DATA_HOME="$xdg_phys"
export USERPROFILE="$home_phys"
exec "$BIN" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prepare one verify run and serve the static garden the way the browser fallback does.
# Invoked by control.sh as LAUNCH_CMD, with PORT, DATA_DIR, BASE_URL, and RUN_ID exported,
# and with the working directory at the repo root.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

: "${PORT:?verify: PORT is required}"
: "${DATA_DIR:?verify: DATA_DIR is required}"

real_home="$(getent passwd "$(id -un)" | awk -F: '{print $6}')"
real_phys="$(cd "$real_home" && pwd -P)"
data_phys="$(cd "$DATA_DIR" && pwd -P)"
if [[ "$data_phys" == "$real_phys" || "$data_phys" == "$real_phys"/* ]]; then
  echo "verify: DATA_DIR is inside the real user home; refusing" >&2
  exit 2
fi

RUN_STATE="$(cd "$(dirname "$DATA_DIR")" && pwd -P)"
SITE="$RUN_STATE/site"
HOME_DIR="$DATA_DIR/home"
XDG_DIR="$DATA_DIR/xdg"
FIXTURE="$DATA_DIR/fixture/events.jsonl"
SUMMARY="$DATA_DIR/garden-summary.json"

mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR" "$XDG_DIR" "$(dirname "$FIXTURE")" "$SITE/web/data"

# Verification scaffolding: a synthetic manual-jsonl source. cleanup deletes RUN_STATE.
cat > "$DATA_DIR/fixture/README.txt" <<'EOF'
Verification scaffolding. One synthetic manual-jsonl row for agent-garden.
control.sh cleanup deletes this run state directory.
EOF

cat > "$FIXTURE" <<'EOF'
{"source":"aider","timestamp":"2026-05-27T12:00:00Z","project_path":"/tmp/verify-garden/demo-plot","session_id":"verify-session-1","event_type":"message","input_tokens":1200,"output_tokens":400,"cache_read_tokens":30,"cache_write_tokens":20,"total_tokens":1650,"tool_calls":3,"model":"manual-model"}
EOF

# Real files only under DATA_DIR, so evidence --copy-data does not follow a tree of symlinks.
# The static site lives beside DATA_DIR and is removed with the run state on cleanup.
link_files() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2" f rel
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    rel="${f#"$src"/}"
    mkdir -p "$dst/$(dirname -- "$rel")"
    ln -sfn "$f" "$dst/$rel"
  done < <(find "$src" -type f -print0)
}

link_files "$REPO_ROOT/web" "$SITE/web"
rm -f "$SITE/web/data/garden-summary.json"
if [[ -d "$REPO_ROOT/assets" ]]; then
  link_files "$REPO_ROOT/assets" "$SITE/assets"
fi

export HOME="$HOME_DIR"
export XDG_DATA_HOME="$XDG_DIR"
export USERPROFILE="$HOME_DIR"

"$SCRIPT_DIR/agent-garden.sh" --manual-jsonl "$FIXTURE" scan
"$SCRIPT_DIR/agent-garden.sh" --manual-jsonl "$FIXTURE" export-web \
  --from-cache "$HOME_DIR/.local-agent-garden/events.json" \
  --out "$SUMMARY"
ln -sfn "$SUMMARY" "$SITE/web/data/garden-summary.json"

echo "verify: serving $SITE on 127.0.0.1:$PORT"
exec python3 -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$SITE"

---
name: verify-pixel-agent-garden
description: "Launch pixel-agent-garden from an empty data dir, drive the agent-garden CLI and the static web fallback over HTTP, and keep evidence under artifacts/verify/. Use for /verify-pixel-agent-garden, before claiming a change works, or to reproduce a bug in the running app."
---

# Verify pixel-agent-garden

Prove behavior on the running app, not a proxy. Every step goes through `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh`, run from the repo root. The map is [FEATURE_MAP.md](FEATURE_MAP.md) and [features/README.md](features/README.md).

Primary surface: the `agent-garden` CLI (`target/debug/agent-garden`, package `local-agent-garden-cli`). Secondary surface: the static `web/` browser fallback, served over HTTP from the run's scratch site. The Tauri desktop shell is not part of this harness.

## Launch

- Build once before the first launch, and only the CLI crate. Do not build `crates/tauri-app`.

  `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build -p local-agent-garden-cli`

- Tests do not replace driving. When you run them, one package at a time: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test -p local-agent-garden-core`, then `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test -p local-agent-garden-cli`.
- `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh launch` starts `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/launch-site.sh` from the repo root on a free port (or `VERIFY_PORT`), with an empty data dir under `${VERIFY_STATE_DIR:-/tmp/verify-pixel-agent-garden-$UID}/<run-id>/data`.
- `scripts/launch-site.sh` is the reproducible fixture. On that empty data dir it writes verification scaffolding at `{DATA_DIR}/fixture/events.jsonl` (one synthetic `aider` row for project `demo-plot`, timestamp `2026-05-27T12:00:00Z`, 1650 tokens), points `HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` at `{DATA_DIR}/home` and `{DATA_DIR}/xdg`, then runs the real CLI: `scan` (cache at `{DATA_DIR}/home/.local-agent-garden/events.json`) and `export-web --out {DATA_DIR}/garden-summary.json`. It serves a scratch copy of `web/` plus `assets/` from the run state directory, with `/web/data/garden-summary.json` linked at that export. Cleanup deletes the scaffolding with the run state.
- Ready means the static garden is usable: `GET /web/index.html` returns 2xx, and doctor proves the seeded summary with `GET /web/data/garden-summary.json`.
- It prints JSON: run_id, pid, port, base_url, data_dir, evidence_dir. The server log is `artifacts/verify/<run-id>/launch.log`.
- It refuses to start while an earlier run in the same state root is alive. Teardown is `cleanup`. Two runs side by side need different `VERIFY_STATE_DIR` values. Never point a run at the real user home or at `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, or `~/.cursor`.

## Doctor

`.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh doctor` is read-only and exits 1 on any failed check: the recorded pid is alive and is still the process this run started, the port answers, `GET /web/index.html` is 2xx, `GET /web/data/garden-summary.json` is 2xx, and the data dir and evidence dir exist. Run it before the first drive and again after any failed drive.

## Drive

- HTTP: `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh drive --feature export-web-summary http GET /web/data/garden-summary.json --expect 200`.
- CLI: `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh drive --feature list-adapters cli -- env HOME={DATA_DIR}/home XDG_DATA_HOME={DATA_DIR}/xdg USERPROFILE={DATA_DIR}/home .claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/agent-garden.sh --manual-jsonl {DATA_DIR}/fixture/events.jsonl adapters --json`. `{DATA_DIR}`, `{PORT}`, `{BASE_URL}`, and `{RUN_ID}` in arguments become this run's values.
- One recipe per feature in `features/`. Drive the public CLI subcommands and the static HTTP paths only. Every CLI argv goes through `scripts/agent-garden.sh`, which exits 2 if `HOME` or `XDG_DATA_HOME` is missing or lies inside the real user home.

## Evidence

- Every drive writes `artifacts/verify/<run-id>/NNN-<feature>-<http|cli>.json`: the request or argv, the status or exit code, the response body or stdout/stderr, and timing.
- `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh evidence --copy-data` snapshots the data dir (the side effect) and writes `manifest.json` with a sha256 per file. The snapshot holds the fixture, `events.json` under the fake home, and `garden-summary.json`. The static site symlinks live beside the data dir and are not the stored side effect.
- Proof standard: the real user path (CLI subcommands and the browser-fallback URLs, no internal setters); the action and the resulting state, read back through a second view; side effects checked, not inferred. This app has no dry-run scan. `scan` always writes the cache under the fake `HOME`.

## Cleanup

`.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh cleanup` stops only the process group this run started (pid file plus recorded start identity, never by name), deletes the scratch state and data dir, and keeps `artifacts/verify/<run-id>/`. It prints the evidence path and fails if the evidence is gone.

## Helpers

- `scripts/control.sh`: `launch | doctor | drive | evidence | cleanup | status | prove`. `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh --help` lists the arguments.
- `scripts/launch-site.sh`: seeds the fixture, runs `scan` and `export-web`, and execs `python3 -m http.server` on `$PORT` bound to `127.0.0.1`. `control.sh launch` is the invocation.
- `scripts/agent-garden.sh`: the only supported way to run the CLI from a recipe. It requires a disposable `HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`. Invocation is the `env HOME={DATA_DIR}/home ... scripts/agent-garden.sh` form in each feature file.
- One-shot proof: `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh prove --feature export-web-summary http GET /web/data/garden-summary.json` runs launch, doctor, drive, evidence, and cleanup, then checks the evidence survived.
- Contract check: `python3 .claude/skills/create-verification-skill/scripts/check_verify_skill.py .claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden`.
- Drift check: `python3 .claude/skills/maintain-verification-skill/scripts/drift_check.py .claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden --repo .`.

# Feature map

The verification map for pixel-agent-garden lives in [features/README.md](features/README.md). Read that index before driving the app, then follow one feature file as the recipe.

The harness covers the `agent-garden` CLI and the static `web/` browser fallback. It does not cover the Tauri desktop shell. The index lists each mapped feature and the reason the desktop shell is unmapped.

# pixel-agent-garden verification map

- Never drive an instance this run did not start.
- Seed data is one synthetic manual JSONL row, written by `scripts/launch-site.sh` during launch, then ingested by the real `scan` and `export-web` commands. The row is source `aider`, project path `/tmp/verify-garden/demo-plot`, session `verify-session-1`, model `manual-model`, timestamp `2026-05-27T12:00:00Z`, 1650 total tokens. Journeys that need a project start from that row.

## Driving conventions

- Run every command from the repo root, literally as written.
- HTTP example: `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh drive --feature export-web-summary http GET /web/data/garden-summary.json --expect 200`.
- CLI example: `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh drive --feature list-adapters cli -- env HOME={DATA_DIR}/home XDG_DATA_HOME={DATA_DIR}/xdg USERPROFILE={DATA_DIR}/home .claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/agent-garden.sh --manual-jsonl {DATA_DIR}/fixture/events.jsonl adapters --json`. `{DATA_DIR}`, `{PORT}`, `{BASE_URL}`, and `{RUN_ID}` in arguments become this run's values.
- Start each recipe from the state its Preconditions name. Use stable handles: subcommand names, JSON fields, URL paths.

## Proof and skip reporting

- Each drive records the action and its result in `artifacts/verify/<run-id>/`.
- A mutation needs a read-only second view (a GET or a list command), then `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh evidence --copy-data` for the stored side effect.
- Record the feature id with every artifact (`--feature`).
- Report an unreachable path with the attempted command and the unmet precondition. Never report it as verified through a different path.

## Feature entry contract

Each feature file has an H1, one paragraph of user-visible behavior, then exactly these H2s in order: `Sub-features`, `How to get to it (user POV)`, `Driving it with control.sh`, `Gotchas`. Keep implementation details out: user paths, stable handles, required state, commands, observable proof.

## Features

- [List local adapters](./list-adapters.md): `agent-garden adapters`.
- [Scan activity into events.json](./scan-events.md): `agent-garden scan`.
- [Show projects](./show-projects.md): `agent-garden projects`, `agent-garden inspect`.
- [Render the ASCII garden](./render-garden.md): `agent-garden garden`.
- [Show one day's token usage](./daily-usage.md): `agent-garden usage`.
- [Estimate local cost](./estimate-cost.md): `agent-garden cost`.
- [Check local garden state](./check-state.md): `agent-garden doctor`.
- [Open the garden in the browser fallback](./export-web-summary.md): `agent-garden export-web`, `GET /web/index.html`, `GET /web/data/garden-summary.json`.

## Not mapped yet

- Tauri desktop shell (tray, native menu, settings persistence, file watcher): driving it requires `crates/tauri-app`, and that crate's webkit system libraries are not installed here. The harness must not build it. The same summary the desktop app shows is covered by the CLI plus the static HTTP fallback.

A user runs `agent-garden doctor` to see whether the garden's own state files and adapter discovery are healthy. Warnings about a first run are still a successful doctor. An invalid cache would fail it. After launch, the fake home has a writable state directory, a one-event cache, and the manual JSONL source active.

## Sub-features

- `check-state-after-launch`: `agent-garden doctor --json` after launch reports `"ok": true`.
- `check-state-text`: `agent-garden doctor` prints the same checks as text and exits 0 when `ok` is true.

## How to get to it (user POV)

- Terminal: `agent-garden --manual-jsonl PATH doctor`.
- Add `--json` for `ok` plus a `checks` array. Each check has `id`, `status`, `message`, and sometimes `detail`.

## Driving it with control.sh

Preconditions:

- `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh doctor` exits 0.
- Fresh launch, and no other summary command (`projects`, `inspect`, `garden`, `cost`, `export-web`) has been driven yet. Launch itself has already run one `scan` and one `export-web`.

- **CLI doctor --json.** Run `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh drive --feature check-state cli -- env HOME={DATA_DIR}/home XDG_DATA_HOME={DATA_DIR}/xdg USERPROFILE={DATA_DIR}/home .claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/agent-garden.sh --manual-jsonl {DATA_DIR}/fixture/events.jsonl doctor --json`. Exit code `0`. `"ok"` is `true`. Check `state_dir` is `ok` with message `state directory is writable`. Check `events_cache` is `ok` with detail `1 events; fingerprint absent`. Check `rings` is `ok` with detail `2 memory events`. Check `adapters` is `ok` with detail `active: manual-jsonl; watch paths: 1`. Check `settings` is `ok` and says `settings.toml is absent; defaults will be used`. Check `prices` is `ok` with detail `35 models; user file absent`. Details that mention a path use the `~/.local-agent-garden` form.
- **CLI doctor.** Run `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh drive --feature check-state cli -- env HOME={DATA_DIR}/home XDG_DATA_HOME={DATA_DIR}/xdg USERPROFILE={DATA_DIR}/home .claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/agent-garden.sh --manual-jsonl {DATA_DIR}/fixture/events.jsonl doctor`. Exit code `0`. The first line is `doctor ok`.
- **Proof.** The text report is the second view of the JSON report. Then run `.claude/skills/verify-pixel-agent-garden/scripts/control.sh evidence --copy-data`. The snapshot contains `home/.local-agent-garden/events.json` and `home/.local-agent-garden/rings.json`, and it does not contain `home/.local-agent-garden/settings.toml` or a user `prices.json`.

- This `doctor` is the product command. The harness health check is `control.sh doctor`. They are different.

- Each later `projects`, `inspect`, `garden`, `cost`, or `export-web` appends ring memory. After those commands, `rings` detail is no longer `2 memory events`. `events_cache` stays `1 events; fingerprint absent`.
- Omitting `--manual-jsonl` makes the adapters check warn `no local adapters discovered` even when the cache file is present.
- Doctor writes a temporary probe inside the state directory only when that directory already exists, and it deletes the probe. The snapshot must not contain a leftover `.doctor-write-` file.
- Every CLI call needs `HOME={DATA_DIR}/home` and `XDG_DATA_HOME={DATA_DIR}/xdg`.
